attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 15 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and the page's own narrative repeats it: «Ήταν 15 Μαΐου». **The one listed line carries two head names** — «Αγια Dymphna» and «Αγιος Gerebernus» — so it is an enumerated pair and therefore two folders, one each. **The page prints her name in two scripts**, Latin in the listing and «Δάφνη» in the body, where it is offered as her name and not as a translation; the Greek form is recorded with that said in its note, and no other language's form is invented from it. **The page grants that she is honoured chiefly in the Western Church** and argues that she is nonetheless an Orthodox saint of the West's Orthodox past; that is the page's own claim and is recorded as such. **Her biography was written in the thirteenth century**, the page says, six centuries after the killing. **No hymn, no relics, no father's name, no name for the kingdom in Ireland.**
